title: EEGManyLabs replication of Vogel & Machizawa (2004), raw BIDS, 304 participants in 10 labs
content:
Raw BIDS EEG from the EEGManyLabs replication of Vogel & Machizawa (2004) change-detection / CDA task,
served from GIN: 304 participants across ten labs (Dartmouth, Florida, Mainz, Muenster, North Dakota, Ohio,
Reykjavik, Sheffield, two Zurich labs). Labs differ in sampling rate (250 to 1024 Hz), channel count
(32 to 129), recording reference and system (Brain Products, EGI, Biosemi, ANT Neuro) and mains frequency.
The CDA recordings total ~150 GB; every file is BrainVision float32 in VECTORIZED order. Four labs have no EOG.
Licence CC BY; cite Strzelczyk et al. (2026, Cortex) and Vogel & Machizawa (2004).

extraction.evidence: README.md, opening paragraph (304 participants, ten labs, GIN link) and section 'The data, and the gate' lab table and 'Streaming, not downloading' (~150 GB)

title: src/splits.py: one seeded subject ordering; BWE split 3 test + 8 train subjects per lab
content:
One deterministic ordering of the 304 subjects shared by every script: per lab, a seeded permutation
(numpy default_rng(0)) over survey.tsv. The first 3 subjects per lab are the held-out BWE test subjects
and the next 8 the BWE training subjects. src/prep.py processes subjects
round-robin across labs in this order. The CDA analyses use every subject that passes exclusion,
regardless of this split; the BWE and spatial-interpolation experiments use it.

extraction.evidence: src/splits.py, module docstring and N_TEST, N_TRAIN = 3, 8; order() uses default_rng(0)

title: src/prep.py: streaming BrainVision reader, CDA epochs and 180 s 250 Hz excerpts
content:
Streams each subject's BrainVision binary off the GIN socket channel by channel (no raw data on disk) and
keeps two products per subject: (1) CDA epochs of lateral posterior pairs plus a horizontal-eye signal
(bipolar HEOG, single HEOG, or F7 - F8 proxy when no EOG) and eye-tracker gaze X where recorded,
resampled to 250 Hz, band-passed 0.1-40 Hz, epoched -0.6..1.4 s around memory-array onset (500 samples),
no re-referencing; (2) a 180 s excerpt of every EEG channel from mid-task, common average reference,
line-noise notches, 0.5 Hz high-pass, 250 Hz. Output is data/prep/<sub>.npz/.json, consumed by the gate,
coherence, BWE, spatial and spectral analyses. Trial artifact rejection is NOT done here (see src/cda.py).

extraction.evidence: src/prep.py, module docstring; process(): HEOG_PAIRS / 'F7-F8 proxy' fallback, band() 0.1 Hz HP + 40 Hz LP, EPOCH = (-150, 350), SR_SEC = 180, 0.5 Hz high-pass; main() uses splits.round_robin

title: src/cda.py: CDA gate with 20 uV eye-step threshold (raised from 12 uV) and subject exclusions
content:
The gate script: per trial, baseline -200..0 ms; reject if the horizontal-eye step (Luck step function,
100 ms windows over -200..1000 ms) exceeds 20 uV on the subject's eye channel, or any lateral channel's
peak-to-peak exceeds 150 uV. One 20 uV threshold is used for bipolar EOG, single EOG and the F7 - F8 proxy;
it was raised from 12 uV after the proxy labs lost a median 75 % of their trials. CDA = contra - ipsi over
the ROI pairs, 300-900 ms; K = N (H - FA) (Cowan). Subjects are excluded with < 50 % clean trials,
accuracy < 0.6, or < 30 clean trials in any set size. The residual lateralized eye signal (heog2/4/6) is
kept per subject in results/subjects.tsv and used only as a robustness filter in src/predict.py.
Its STEP_THR and ROI are also imported by src/cohere.py and src/trials.py.

extraction.evidence: src/cda.py, module docstring (threshold raised from 12 uV, 75 % rejection, exclusion rules) and STEP_THR / WIN constants; main() writes subjects.tsv with the excluded flag

title: src/lisa_eeg.py: LISA / LISAS and arm losses ported verbatim from lisa-rtm to 250 Hz EEG
content:
LISA (deterministic local-implicit super-resolution) and LISAS (same 88k-parameter network with 8 Gaussian
noise channels trained under the energy score), the arm losses det / det_paper / es_marg, the multi-scale
STFT loss and the scoring utilities (snr_db, third-octave edges, CRPS ensemble, PIT ranks, spread-skill),
copied from lisa-rtm commit cb304b7. Only configuration changes: fs_hi 48 kHz -> 250 Hz and n_fft
2048 -> 256 with STFT scales (256, 64), (128, 32), (64, 16).

extraction.evidence: src/lisa_eeg.py, module docstring listing the lisa-rtm source file of every definition and the changed configuration

title: src/predict.py: leave-one-lab-out Gaussian CRPS forecaster of capacity K, with --strict-eye option
content:
Scores a CDA feature as a forecaster of Cowan's K the way lisa-rtm scores a sampler: leave one lab out,
fit OLS on nine labs, issue a Gaussian forecast for each subject of the tenth, and compute closed-form CRPS
against climatology (nine-lab K distribution) and a lab-oracle reference (held-out lab's own mean K),
plus PIT coverage, point-forecast spread sd(mu)/sd(K) and split-half reliability. Features: cda4, cda46,
cda4m2, cda_slope. With --strict-eye it drops subjects whose residual HEOG (max |heog2/4/6|) exceeds the
75th percentile of included subjects and writes to results/strict_eye/. Its crps_gauss is reused by
src/ideas/eyes.py.

extraction.evidence: src/predict.py, module docstring (CRPS formula, clim / lab_clim / cda / cda_labc) and main(): '--strict-eye' branch with quantile(0.75)

title: src/trials.py: per-trial table (trials.csv.gz) behind every 'ideas' analysis
content:
Builds one row per trial for every included subject (subjects.tsv excluded == False): set size, side,
outcome, correct, RT, a clean flag using cda.py's eye-step and amplitude criteria, single-trial CDA
(300-900 ms), late CDA, alpha lateralization, pre-stimulus alpha, toward-cue HEOG, gaze shift, and
lag-1 autocorrelation / variance of the lateralized signal. Output results/trials.csv.gz is not tracked in
git; hysteresis, ews, eyes, trial_forecast, hmm_states and extra all read it.

extraction.evidence: src/trials.py, module docstring (column list) and main(): reads subjects.tsv, filters ~S.excluded, imports STEP_THR from cda, writes trials.csv.gz

title: CDA gate passes: 248 subjects, CDA -0.50/-0.79/-0.75 uV at set sizes 2/4/6, 4 vs 2 t = -7.90
content:
Running src/cda.py on all prepped subjects leaves n = 248 subjects in 10 labs after exclusion. The grand
CDA is -0.497 / -0.794 / -0.747 uV at set sizes 2 / 4 / 6 and K is 1.71 / 2.41 / 2.26, so the classic
shape (rise to capacity, flat beyond) appears; CDA 4 vs 2 gives t = -7.90, p = 9.2e-14. Split-half
reliability (Spearman-Brown) is 0.83 for cda4 but only 0.35 for the 2->4 difference score. This gate
output (results/subjects.tsv) is the input of every downstream CDA, coherence, prediction and ideas analysis.
hypothesis: The pipeline reproduces a CDA that rises with load to capacity before any lisa-rtm method is applied.

extraction.evidence: results/tables.md, section 'CDA -> K': 'n = 248 subjects, 10 labs', the 'Split-half reliability' line and the 'Set size: CDA ... K ... t = -7.90' line

title: BWE training: three LISA/LISAS arms on identical batches, 6000 CPU steps, 62.5 -> 250 Hz
content:
Paired training of three arms of the ported LISA/LISAS (det_paper = L1 only, det = L1 + 0.1 MSSTFT,
es_marg = energy-score sampler) on a corpus of 80 BWE training subjects, 960 channel recordings, 48.0 h,
LISAS with 87,777 parameters. The log ends at step 5999/6000 after 2121 s with losses det_paper 0.2290,
det 0.3588, es_marg 0.2114. One seed; lambda = 0.1 not tuned. The three checkpoints (results/bwe/*.pt)
and the high-band PSD for the shaped-noise control are this run's outputs.

extraction.evidence: results/bwe/train.log, last line 'step 5999/6000 [ 2121s] det_paper: 0.2290 ... det: 0.3588 ... es_marg: 0.2114'

title: BWE det_paper (L1 only, LISA's released loss) leaves the high band 23.3 dB short
content:
The deterministic L1-only arm, scored on the held-out BWE subjects, has a high-band deficit of
-23.32 dB, CRPS 2.901, coherent fraction above 40 Hz 0.002 and SNR 0.12 dB under the naive-interpolator
ceiling. It reproduces the audio paper's L1 muffling on EEG: the missing high band is incoherent
with the low band, so a conditional-mean model outputs almost nothing there.
hypothesis: The lisa-rtm audio pattern (L1 muffles the missing band) reproduces on EEG.

extraction.evidence: results/tables.md, section 'BWE', row 'det_paper: L1 only (LISA's released loss)'

title: BWE det (L1 + 0.1 MSSTFT) recovers most of the deficit to -7.8 dB, CRPS 1.170
content:
Adding the multi-scale STFT term (lambda 0.1) to the deterministic arm cuts the high-band deficit to
-7.82 dB with CRPS 1.170, but the coherent fraction above 40 Hz stays 0.001 and SNR drops 0.91 dB below
the ceiling: the restored energy is not aligned with the truth. Scored on the held-out BWE subjects.
hypothesis: A spectral loss term restores high-band level without restoring information.

extraction.evidence: results/tables.md, section 'BWE', row 'det: L1 + 0.1 MSSTFT'

title: BWE es_marg energy-score sampler: deficit -2.1 dB, CRPS 0.673, but truth above all draws 32 %
content:
The LISAS energy-score sampler (M = 8 draws), on the held-out BWE subjects: one draw has a deficit of
-2.08 dB and the best CRPS (0.673); its tau = 0 mean is -10.89 dB. Coherent fraction above 40 Hz is 0.001
and SNR is 3.71 dB under the ceiling, the identity's price for a level-correct incoherent band. PIT
low/high tails are 0.098 / 0.316 against an ideal 0.111: a residual level bias, not a narrow ensemble
(gap 2.66 dB vs 2.91 independent). Same pattern as the audio sampler.
hypothesis: The energy-score sampler closes the level gap that L1 leaves, as in lisa-rtm audio.

extraction.evidence: results/tables.md, section 'BWE', rows 'es_marg at tau = 0' and 'es_marg: energy score, one draw (M = 8)'

title: BWE control: unconditional shaped noise CRPS 0.801, envelope r 0.037 (sampler beats it)
content:
Unconditional noise shaped to the training high-band mean spectrum (M = 8), scored like the samplers on
the held-out BWE subjects: deficit +4.25 dB, CRPS 0.801 (worse than es_marg's 0.673), PIT low/high
0.368 / 0.081, and its frame envelope does not track the truth (r = 0.037, slope 0.013). This control
shows the es_marg sampler uses its input through the envelope rather than only matching level.

extraction.evidence: results/tables.md, section 'BWE', row 'shaped noise: unconditional, mean HB spectrum (M = 8)' and the envelope table row of the same name

title: High-band envelope is predictable from the low band (within-recording r = 0.574)
content:
A ridge regression on low-band log band energies, trained on training subjects and applied to held-out
ones, predicts the high-band frame envelope with pooled R^2 0.529 and within-recording r = 0.574
(R^2 0.289) over 83160 frames. The high-band waveform is incoherent but its envelope is not; the
es_marg tau = 0 output tracks it at r = 0.583 and shaped noise at r = 0.037.

config.model: ridge on low-band log band energies

extraction.evidence: results/bwe/score_extra.json, keys env_pred_from_lb and env_regression_within_item ('es_marg tau0', 'shaped_noise')

title: CDA is a conditional mean carrying 2 % of single-trial energy; alpha envelope 9x more coherent than waveform
content:
Scoring the leave-one-out set-size mean as a point predictor of each single trial's lateralized signal
(lisa-rtm identity), on 248 subjects in the gate's CDA window: broadband coherent fraction c = 0.0200 (t = 11.3),
concentrated below 2 Hz (c = 0.0431). Alpha (8-13 Hz) waveform c is 0.0024 but the alpha envelope
(log contra - ipsi power) has c = 0.0216, and alpha lateralization is -0.085 (t = -13.7).
Evoked and induced lateralization get one number on one scale.
hypothesis: The trial-averaged CDA is lisa-rtm's deterministic point model; an incoherent band can have a predictable envelope.

extraction.evidence: results/coherence_summary.json, summary keys c_time, c_0-2, cwave_alpha 8-13, cenv_alpha 8-13, ali_alpha 8-13; n_subjects 248

title: Missing-electrode interpolation: Wiener muffled by its coherent fraction above 30 Hz; spline worst
content:
On the 30 held-out BWE subjects, every 10-05-labelled electrode was predicted from the others by spherical
spline, a per-band Wiener filter (fit on the first half of the excerpt, scored on the second) and one Gaussian conditional draw.
Below 13 Hz Wiener c is 0.951 (8-13 Hz); at 30-60 Hz c = 0.570 with p = 0.587, so the MSE-optimal map is
muffled by exactly its coherent fraction. The Gaussian draw restores p to 0.998 but SNR falls to 0.969 dB
(Wiener 3.532 dB). Spline is worst: c = 0.429, SNR 0.735 dB at 30-60 Hz. Template positions, not digitized.
hypothesis: The lisa-rtm identity (p = c for the MSE optimum) holds in space for a missing electrode.

extraction.evidence: results/spatial_summary.json, median.wiener / median.sampler / median.spline at bands 8-13 and 30-60; n_subjects 30 (values rounded here to 3 dp)

title: CDA forecasts K in an unseen lab: CRPSS +5.8 %, but lab-centred only +0.7 % vs lab oracle +15.8 %
content:
Leave-one-lab-out Gaussian forecasts of K on 248 subjects in 10 labs. The CDA mean of set sizes 4 and 6
gives CRPS skill +0.058 [0.022, 0.094] over climatology (r = -0.333, within-lab r = -0.195). Centring the
CDA within lab removes it (+0.0071), while knowing only the lab (oracle) is worth +0.158. So the CDA-K
link is mostly between labs. cda4 gives +0.042 and cda_slope +0.051.
hypothesis: The CDA predicts an individual's working-memory capacity K (Vogel & Machizawa 2004), even in a lab never seen.

extraction.evidence: results/predict.json, features.cda46.scores (cda / cda_labc / lab_clim crpss_vs_clim, crpss_ci95), features.cda46.r and r_within_lab; features.cda4 and cda_slope

title: The original's CDA 2->4 difference score is the weakest predictor: CRPSS CI includes 0, reliability 0.35
content:
In the same leave-one-lab-out scoring on 248 subjects, the CDA increase from set size 2 to 4 (Vogel &
Machizawa's predictor) has r = -0.226 with K, CRPS skill +0.0258 with 95 % CI [-0.0035, 0.0558], and
negative skill once centred in lab (-0.0036). Its split-half reliability (Spearman-Brown) is 0.348
against 0.828 for the set-size-4 amplitude, so it cannot carry an individual difference.
hypothesis: The difference score used by the original study is a good individual-capacity predictor.

extraction.evidence: results/predict.json, features.cda4m2 (r, scores.cda.crpss_vs_clim, crpss_ci95, scores.cda_labc) and reliability.cda46_minus_2 / cda4 spearman_brown

title: Strict-eye rerun (top-quartile residual HEOG dropped, n = 186): cda46 skill +5.2 % holds, cda4 CI now crosses 0
content:
Robustness rerun of the CDA -> K forecast (src/predict.py --strict-eye) dropping the quarter of subjects
with the largest residual lateralized eye signal from the cda.py gate, leaving 186 subjects in 10 labs.
cda46 keeps CRPS skill +0.0523 [0.0049, 0.0985] (lab-centred +0.0036, lab oracle +0.164), r = -0.332.
But cda4 (+0.0353, CI [-0.0056, 0.0740]) and cda_slope (+0.0387, CI [-0.0036, 0.0772]) lose significance,
so "all of it holds" applies to the main feature only. Set-size CDA is -0.456 / -0.730 / -0.674 uV.
hypothesis: The CDA-K forecast is not driven by residual eye movements that the 20 uV eye-step threshold let through.

config.filter: drop top quartile of residual HEOG among included subjects

extraction.evidence: results/strict_eye/predict.json, n 186; features.cda46 / cda4 / cda_slope scores (crpss_vs_clim, crpss_ci95); set_size; cda4_vs_cda2.t

title: Capacity signal is mostly engagement: lab-mean attention vs K r = +0.90
content:
Cowan's K was split into attention a = K2/2 (lapses on 2-item trials) and capacity on attended trials K/a,
for 248 subjects. Across the 10 labs, lab-mean attention and lab-mean K correlate at r = +0.895, and the
lab-mean CDA correlates with K at -0.855 and with attention at -0.850. Within labs, regressing the CDA on
both components gives attention the larger unique share (beta -0.157 vs -0.108, se 0.065). Reading:
much of what the CDA tracks as "capacity" is engagement. Later weakened by the HMM engagement-state test.
hypothesis: Much of what is called working-memory capacity, and what the CDA tracks, is how engaged the person was.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/engagement.json, lab_level.attn_K / K / attn and within_lab.beta_attn / beta_Kc

title: Idea: GLM-HMM engagement states would turn the attention split into a per-trial state estimate
content:
Listed as an untested idea in IDEAS.md: GLM-HMM engagement states (Ashwood et al. 2022) as a model-based
version of the attention split, scored by Brier decomposition, turning the engagement headline into a
per-trial state estimate. It was tested overnight as a 2-state HMM (see hmm-engagement-states).
hypothesis: Trial-by-trial engagement states exist and explain capacity / CDA variation better than an i.i.d. model.

extraction.evidence: IDEAS.md, 'Ideas from the literature not yet tested', item 3

title: 2-state engagement HMM: no held-out gain over i.i.d., CDA unchanged in disengaged stretches
content:
A 2-state HMM over trial outcomes per subject (248 subjects) gives no held-out log-likelihood gain over an
i.i.d. model (+0.00089 per trial, p = 0.38; 43 % of subjects better). The CDA does not differ between
disengaged and engaged stretches (t = 0.035, n = 209), although RT is slower (t = 8.28) and pre-stimulus
alpha lower (t = -5.51) when disengaged. Within lab, CDA vs engaged-state K r = -0.084 (p = 0.19).
This weakens the engagement headline: the 2-item attention score is not momentary engagement.
hypothesis: Trial-by-trial engagement states exist and explain capacity / CDA variation better than an i.i.d. model.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/hmm.json, heldout_dll_per_trial, cda_dis_minus_eng, rt_dis_minus_eng, alpha_pre_dis_minus_eng, cda_vs_Keng

title: Single-trial EEG/eye readout has zero forecast value for correctness (Brier skill ~0)
content:
Forecasting whether each trial is answered correctly from the person's own accuracy at that load, then
adding single-trial CDA, late CDA, alpha lateralization, pre-stimulus alpha and HEOG (fit on nine labs,
scored on the tenth), over 144831 trials of 248 subjects: Brier skill 1.07e-05 with 95 % CI
[-0.00022, 0.00024]. The CDA coefficient has the published sign (-0.062), but per trial it buys nothing,
consistent with the low single-trial coherent fraction of the CDA.
hypothesis: The single-trial CDA / alpha / eye signal forecasts whether this trial will be correct.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/trial_forecast.json, keys bss, ci95, n_trials, coef_mean.cda

title: Load hysteresis: after a 6-item trial CDA larger, RT 16 ms faster; direct 4-after-6 contrast n.s.
content:
Per-subject OLS of trial measures on current-load, previous-load and side-repeat dummies (trials.csv.gz).
A previous 6-item trial shifts the CDA by -0.087 uV (p = 0.012, same sign in 10/10 labs; 0.29 of the
current 2->4 effect) and speeds RT by 16.4 ms (t = -7.96, 10/10 labs). When the cued side repeats,
pre-stimulus alpha lateralization is higher (t = +7.93). But the direct contrast "load 4 after 6 minus load 4
after 2" on the CDA is n.s. (p = 0.45). Exploratory (IDEAS.md: not family-wise corrected).
hypothesis: The previous trial's memory load shifts the current trial in brain and behaviour (an attractor or lingering trace).

config.model: per-subject OLS with current/previous load dummies

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/hysteresis.json, keys cda:prev6, cda:prev6_over_cur4, rt:prev6, alpha_pre_lat:same_side, cda:4after6-4after2 (IDEAS.md prose quotes a different 2-after-6 figure not in this file)

title: Hysteresis split-half replication: significant in one random half (p = 0.0003), not the other (p = 0.50)
content:
Replication of the CDA load-hysteresis effect by splitting the subjects into two random halves of 124:
half 2 shows mean -0.267 (t = -3.74, p = 0.00028) but half 1 only -0.054 (t = -0.68, p = 0.50). The sign
is negative in 9 of 10 labs. Verdict in IDEAS.md: suggestive.
hypothesis: The CDA load-hysteresis effect replicates in independent subsets.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/extra.json, hysteresis_halves (half 1 / half 2) and hysteresis_labs_negative

title: Capacity as a bifurcation: no single-trial CDA variability peak at load = K (p = 0.12)
content:
Tested whether within-person single-trial CDA variability peaks where load meets the person's own capacity
(load - K near 0), as a bifurcation would predict. The per-person quadratic curvature of CDA SD in
(load - K) is -0.0096 (t = -1.55, p = 0.12): no peak.
hypothesis: Working-memory capacity behaves like a bifurcation, with a variability peak at load = K.

config.measure: within-person single-trial CDA SD by load - K

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/extra.json, bifurcation and bifurcation_quadratic

title: Depletion: recent load does not predict errors beyond time on task (p = 0.085)
content:
Per-subject logistic regression of errors on time on task and the mean set size of the previous 10 trials.
Time on task is strongly negative for errors (t = -8.39) while recent load adds +0.012 (t = 1.73,
p = 0.085). No depletion effect beyond time on task.
hypothesis: Recent memory load depletes resources and predicts errors beyond time on task.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/extra.json, keys 'error_logit_recent load (last 10 trials)' and 'error_logit_time on task'

title: Lapse early warnings, not detrended: pre-stimulus alpha looks lower before lapses (t = -5.31) - a confound
content:
Early-warning signals in the 10 trials before a lapse (error on a 2-item trial) vs correct 2-item trials of
the same person, 231 subjects, without removing time-on-task trends. Pre-stimulus alpha is lower before
lapses (t = -5.31, p = 2.6e-07), RT variance higher (t = 4.08) and RT slower (t = 5.41). The alpha
precursor disappears after detrending (ews-lapses-detrended): lapses cluster early in the session, when
alpha is lower. A cautionary negative result.
hypothesis: Working-memory lapses are preceded by critical slowing down and a pre-stimulus alpha precursor.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/ews_W10.json, keys alpha_pre:mean, rt:var, rt:mean, n_subjects

title: Lapses after detrending: RT variance rises (t = 4.09), no autocorrelation rise, no EEG precursor
content:
Same lapse early-warning test with time-on-task trends removed (231 subjects, 10-trial window). RT variance
still rises before lapses (t = 4.09) and RT is slightly faster (-6.7 ms, t = -2.96), but lag-1
autocorrelation does not rise (t = 1.57) and the pre-stimulus alpha effect vanishes (t = -0.61, p = 0.54);
CDA mean/var/ac1 show nothing. Lapses look like flickering, not critical slowing down; a behavioural early
warning exists, a neural one does not.
hypothesis: Working-memory lapses are preceded by critical slowing down and a pre-stimulus alpha precursor.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/ews_W10_detrend.json, keys rt:var, rt:mean, rt:ac1, alpha_pre:mean, detrend: true

title: Eye drift predicts K within lab as well as the CDA (gaze slope r = +0.21) and is equally useless out of lab
content:
Toward-cue eye drift during retention (HEOG for 248 subjects; eye-tracker gaze for 110 subjects in 4 labs)
vs the CDA as predictors of K. Gaze drift slope correlates with K within lab at r = +0.214 (p = 0.025) but
its leave-one-lab-out CRPS skill is 0.009 with CI [-0.038, 0.051]. Controlling for HEOG drift leaves the
CDA-K link essentially unchanged (-0.191 -> -0.178). Replicates Kang & Woodman 2014: gaze bias scales
with load but neither produces the CDA nor predicts K.
hypothesis: The eyes, not the brain, carry the CDA's capacity signal.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/eyes.json, keys gaze_slope, cda46, cda_K, partial_cda_K_given_heog

title: Idea: aperiodic (1/f) exponent as an independent capacity predictor (Virtue-Griffiths 2025, r ~ 0.28)
content:
Listed as untested in IDEAS.md: the aperiodic exponent during the delay as an independent capacity
predictor, after Virtue-Griffiths et al. 2025 who report r ~ 0.28 (n = 84), testable from the 180 s
excerpt with specparam. Also listed: criticality (DFA of the alpha envelope) as a trait.
hypothesis: The aperiodic exponent (and alpha DFA) predicts working-memory capacity K independently of the CDA.

extraction.evidence: IDEAS.md, 'Ideas from the literature not yet tested', items 1 and 2

title: Resting spectral traits (1/f exponent, IAF, alpha power, DFA, HF floor) do not predict K within lab
content:
FOOOF fits on each included subject's resting excerpt (248 subjects, median fit R^2 0.994). Within lab, none
of the traits predicts K: exponent r = -0.082 (p = 0.20), offset -0.066, individual alpha frequency +0.065,
alpha peak power -0.105, alpha DFA -0.092, high-frequency floor +0.055. The traits do decode lab above
chance (0.216 vs 0.145), i.e. they mostly carry hardware/lab differences.
hypothesis: The aperiodic exponent (and alpha DFA) predicts working-memory capacity K independently of the CDA.

extraction.evidence: results/ideas/spectral.json, exponent / offset / iaf / alpha_peak_pow / dfa_alpha / hf_floor r_K_within, lab_decoding_accuracy, chance

title: Untested: is the CDA produced by asymmetric alpha amplitude modulation (baseline shift)?
content:
Listed as untested in IDEAS.md (Nikulin; van Dijk et al. 2010): whether the CDA is a baseline shift
from asymmetric alpha amplitude modulation. It needs the excerpt's low-frequency content, which the
0.5 Hz high-pass in preprocessing limits. A related open question is whether the between-lab CDA
difference is hardware (ROI composition differs by montage).
hypothesis: The CDA is produced by asymmetric alpha amplitude modulation rather than a separate sustained negativity.

extraction.evidence: IDEAS.md, 'Ideas from the literature not yet tested', items 4 and 5

title: Verdict: lisa-rtm diagnostics and proper scoring transfer to EEG; the BWE network solves no real problem
content:
The README verdict table across the four experiments: LISA/LISAS run unchanged on EEG (87,777 parameters,
35 min on 4 CPU cores) and reproduce the audio result (L1 23 dB short, energy score to -2 dB, c <= 0.002

title: Ideas verdict: CDA 'capacity' is partly engagement; single-trial, lapse-precursor, spectral and bifurcation tests null
content:
IDEAS.md summary over 248 subjects (176,917 trials): the headline was that the capacity signal is mostly
engagement (lab-mean attention vs K +0.90), later weakened by the 2-state HMM (no held-out gain, CDA unchanged
in disengaged stretches). Single-trial brain-reading has zero forecast value (Brier skill +0.00 %).
Load hysteresis is exploratory and only suggestive on split-half replication. Lapses show behavioural
flickering (RT variance up) but no neural precursor once time on task is removed. Eyes predict K as weakly
as the CDA. Spectral traits, capacity-as-bifurcation and depletion are all null.
